stage1.impression: A cluttered back-bar wall of flat, identically labelled CG bottles under cold blue-white shelf light, with a cream speaker cabinet and a floating clear hood boxed into a dark niche in the centre. The bottles out-shine and out-number the product, the light splits into cold blue on the left and warm on the right, and the foreground counter is a dim slab with a hard diagonal colour seam. It reads as a competent game-engine interior, not a magazine photograph.

blocking_9: The speaker must be the brightest, most saturated-to-true object in frame: batts and acrylic brighter than every shelf (shelf lum_median below the speaker face's).
Bottles must read as real glass with liquid, varied labels and varied models; no repeated twine-wrap label on every bottle.
One coherent colour world: a single warm shelf/niche temperature, no cold-blue left half against a warm right half.
The foreground counter must read as honed stone with a soft, believable reflection, not a dark slab with a hard blue/warm diagonal seam.
Fewer bottles, with negative space and room for type around the hero.
Neutral grade on the Fog speaker: whites read clear-white, not yellow-green, and the woofer is not crushed to a blue-less black.

defects.what: Left shelves lit cold blue-white (b 202 vs r 139), brighter than the product (lum_median 173).
Right shelves warm, contradicting the cold left side: two colour temperatures in one wall.
Bottles are low-detail CG: flat glass, no liquid refraction, the same twine-wrap label repeated on nearly every bottle, repeated models.
Foreground counter: blue reflection on the left meets warm on the right along a hard diagonal near x 430; surface reads as flat dark plastic, no honed-stone texture.
Saturated red strip at the top of the niche (r 92, g 15) reads as a stray light leak.
Niche back panel is a flat bright grey (lum 106) that competes with the clear hood; the hood's outline is weak against it.
Cream batts carry a yellow-green cast (r 131, g 119, b 83): the Fog speaker does not read clear-white.
Woofer cone crushed with blue channel near zero (b 1): muddy, detail-less black.
Speaker base sits in shadow with no visible contact shadow or light cast onto its plinth; weight is unclear.
No atmosphere: nearly no haze, everything at the same sharpness, so no depth between niche, shelves and counter.

changes.problem: The bottle shelves are the brightest thing in the frame, so the speaker is not the hero.

evidence.measured: lum_median 172.8 on the left shelves vs 119.2 on the speaker's batts (470,360,690,430).

changes.expected: Shelves drop to a glow around lum 100-115, below the speaker face; bottles become a backdrop.

changes.problem: The Fog speaker is underlit relative to its setting and its face reads dull cream.

evidence.measured: lum_median 119.2; batts below the shelf level.

change.setting: on each Fog speaker 2 x spot
change.to: 320.0 W, cone 30 deg, aimed at the cabinet's mid-height so light passes through the acrylic onto the batts

changes.expected: Batts read bright, clean white at lum ~160-185, the brightest surface in frame without clipping; the acrylic edges catch a highlight.

changes.problem: The left half of the back-bar is cold blue and the right half warm, so the wall has no single colour world.

evidence.measured: left shelves r 139 / g 179 / b 202; right shelves (800,30,1180,170) r 155 / g 139 / b 133.

change.from: cold white on the left run, warm on the right
change.to: one warm 2700 K on every shelf run, matching the right side

changes.expected: Both shelf runs share a warm amber tone; blue no longer dominates the left.

changes.problem: The grade puts a yellow-green cast on the clear-white speaker and crushes the woofer's blue channel.

evidence.measured: woofer r 19 / g 16 / b 1; batts r 131 / g 119 / b 83.

changes.expected: Batts read near neutral white (b within ~25 of r); the woofer holds dark neutral detail rather than olive-black.

changes.problem: The foreground counter is a dark slab split by a hard diagonal between a blue reflection and warm light.

evidence.measured: left counter r 37 / g 57 / b 65 (lum 53) vs right (500,640,1200,800) r 36 / g 27 / b 13 (lum 28); 58 px transition near x 430.

change.to: 200.0 W, cone 45 deg, with one centred in front of the Fog niche so its pool lands on the counter in the lower third

changes.expected: A soft warm pool across the counter in front of the speaker; the blue left reflection fades (with c1/c3) and the seam disappears.

changes.problem: The bottles read as CG: identical twine labels, repeated models, flat glass with no liquid.

evidence.measured: seen: the same wrapped label on about 90 % of the bottles; no refraction or meniscus.

change.from: about 70 bottles from a few models with one label
change.to: about 35 bottles from 12+ distinct scanned models, real glass IOR 1.5 with liquid volumes, varied paper labels; leave gaps on the shelves either side of the niche

changes.expected: Bottles read as a real collection; negative space opens around the speaker.

changes.problem: A saturated red line at the top of the niche reads as a light leak.

change.setting: the red source above the Fog niche (back-bar back panel / niche edge)
change.to: off, or the same warm 2700 K as the niches at 30 % of its level

changes.expected: The top of the niche reads as a dark, quiet frame edge.

changes.problem: There is no atmosphere, so the niche, shelves and counter have no depth between them.

evidence.measured: seen: equal sharpness and contrast at every depth; no visible beams from the spots.

change.setting: haze in the room's air density

changes.expected: Faint visible cones from the Fog spots and a slight veil over the far shelves, separating the hero from the wall.

out_of_scope.request: The clear hood floats above the cabinet on two thin posts and reads as a separate object, as if it were detached from the speaker.
out_of_scope.why: It is the product's own part (shape and parts are fixed).

out_of_scope.request: The card says the frame is for the Fog pair, but only one speaker shows; reframing to hold both niches would change the composition substantially.
out_of_scope.why: This is a camera/brief question for the art director: whether the shot is one speaker or the pair. Pixel tests do not apply after a camera move.

out_of_scope.request: Honed dark stone counter could take more visible texture.
out_of_scope.why: The bar top's material is fixed by the room's design; only its lighting is changed here (c5).
